title: Bounded normalized integral for complete scalars on pro-prime-to-ell groups
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a complete nonarchimedean normed field $B$ containing $\mathbf Q_\ell$ isometrically [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]; thus $|x+y|\leq\max(|x|,|y|)$ and every Cauchy sequence converges in $B$. Let $K$ be a profinite group (a compact Hausdorff topological group with a basis of open normal subgroups), all of whose finite continuous quotient groups have order prime to $\ell$. Write $C(P,B)$ for all continuous maps from a profinite space $P$ to $B$, and give $C(K,B)$ the supremum norm. There exists a $B$-linear map
$$I_K:C(K,B)\longrightarrow B$$
with $|I_K(f)|\leq\sup_{h\in K}|f(h)|$, $I_K(1)=1$, and $I_K(h\mapsto f(ah))=I_K(f)=I_K(h\mapsto f(ha))$ for all $a\in K$. For every open normal $U\subseteq K$ and every function $f$ factoring through $Q=K/U$,
$$I_K(f)=|Q|^{-1}\sum_{q\in Q}f(q).$$
For every profinite space $P$ and every $f\in C(P\times K,B)$, the function $p\mapsto I_K(h\mapsto f(p,h))$ is continuous. This operation is $C(P,B)$-linear and commutes with precomposition by every continuous map $P'\to P$. It also commutes with finite sums. All spaces lie in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: For each open normal subgroup $U$, the open cosets cover compact $K$, hence a finite subcover contains every coset; thus $Q_U=K/U$ is finite and nonempty. Let $D\subseteq C(K,B)$ consist of the functions factoring through some $Q_U$. These are continuous because cosets are open. Intersecting two open normal subgroups gives another such subgroup, and both quotient maps factor through its quotient. Consequently pointwise sums and scalar multiples make $D$ a $B$-linear subspace; constant functions belong to it. Write $A_U(\bar f)=|Q_U|^{-1}\sum_{q\in Q_U}\bar f(q)$ for the proposed average of a function factoring through $Q_U$. The denominators are nonzero because $B$ contains the characteristic-zero field $\mathbf Q_\ell$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image scalar tame-kernel input; agent analytic expansion: finite quotient functions and the candidate averaging formula. The blueprint provides the context, not this argument.

proof.text:
Suppose $V\subseteq U$ are open normal subgroups. The map $Q_V\to Q_U$ is onto and each fibre has $t=|U/V|$ points: choose a representative $a$ of a coset of $U$; the bijection $U/V\to aU/V$ is $uV\mapsto auV$. Partitioning the finite sum by these fibres gives $|Q_V|=t|Q_U|$ and
$$|Q_V|^{-1}\sum_{z\in Q_V}\bar f(z\bmod U)=(t|Q_U|)^{-1}t\sum_{q\in Q_U}\bar f(q)=A_U(\bar f).$$
For two arbitrary choices $U_1,U_2$ through which the same function factors, apply this identity to $V=U_1\cap U_2$. The descended functions on $Q_V$ agree since $K\to Q_V$ is onto. Thus $A:D\to B$ is well defined. Computing two functions on a common quotient proves additivity and $B$-homogeneity term by term.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image scalar tame-kernel input; agent analytic expansion: independence under refinement of the finite quotient. The blueprint provides the context, not this argument.

proof.text:
For $n=|Q_U|$, the prime-to-$\ell$ hypothesis gives $v_\ell(n)=0$ directly from the valuation formula of [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Thus $|n|_B=|n|_\ell=1$ by the isometric inclusion, and $|n^{-1}|_B=1$ by multiplicativity. Induction on the finite number of summands using the strong triangle inequality gives
$$|A(f)|\leq\max_{q\in Q_U}|\bar f(q)|=\|f\|_\infty.$$
Also $A(1)=n^{-1}n=1$. For $a\in K$, normality of $U$ makes both $q\mapsto aq$ and $q\mapsto qa$ permutations of $Q_U$. Reindexing the finite sum proves $A(f(a\cdot))=A(f)=A(f(\cdot a))$. The norm identity uses only the definition of the valuation, rather than introducing a separate node for a prime-to-$\ell$ integer.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image scalar tame-kernel input; agent analytic expansion: contractivity, normalization and both finite-level translation identities. The blueprint provides the context, not this argument.

proof.text: The open normal subgroups and their cosets are clopen: the complement of a coset is the union of all other open cosets. They separate distinct points by Hausdorffness and the assumed identity-neighbourhood basis. A connected subset containing two distinct points would therefore be separated by a clopen coset. Hence $K$ is totally disconnected. Given $f\in C(K,B)$ and $\epsilon>0$, apply [lem-sfb-profinite-finite-map-approximation] with $X=K$, $V=B$ and the open neighbourhood $S=\{(b,c):|b-c|<\epsilon/2\}$ of the diagonal. Obtain continuous $g:K\to\operatorname{Fin}(n)$ and $h$ with $|f(x)-h(g(x))|<\epsilon/2$. Put $d=h\circ g$, which is continuous since the intermediate space is discrete. We next check explicitly that $d\in D$, so that these approximations prove norm density.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image scalar tame-kernel input; agent analytic expansion: apply finite-map approximation with an arbitrarily small norm error. The blueprint provides the context, not this argument.

proof.text: For each $x\in K$, the open fibre $g^{-1}(g(x))$ contains $xU_x$ for some open normal subgroup $U_x$, by the identity-neighbourhood basis translated by $x$. Choose a finite subcover $x_iU_{x_i}$ of $K$, and put $U=\bigcap_iU_{x_i}$. If $y\in x_iU_{x_i}$ and $u\in U$, then $yu\in x_iU_{x_i}$, so $g(yu)=g(y)$. Thus $g$, and therefore $d$, is constant on every coset $yU$, giving $d\in D$. The pointwise approximation implies $\|f-d\|_\infty\leq\epsilon/2<\epsilon$. This proves density for every $f,\epsilon$, without a countable basis or metrizability assumption on $K$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image scalar tame-kernel input; agent analytic expansion: finite-subcover verification that the approximation descends to an open-normal quotient. The blueprint provides the context, not this argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dense-subspace-contractive-extension] with scalar field $k=B$, normed space $E=C(K,B)$, complete target $F=B$, dense subspace $D$ from steps 1 and 4–5, and $u=A$ from steps 2–3. The supremum norm is the norm stipulated in the statement; its triangle inequality and scalar homogeneity follow pointwise from those in $B$. Completeness is required only for the target $B$, which is a hypothesis of the item. This produces a continuous $B$-linear extension $I_K$ with $|I_K(f)|\leq\|f\|_\infty$. Its agreement with $A$ gives the required formula on every $K/U$, in particular $I_K(1)=1$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image scalar tame-kernel input; agent analytic expansion: extend the finite-quotient functional over complete scalars. The blueprint provides the context, not this argument.

proof.text: Fix $a\in K$. The maps $T_a^Lf(h)=f(ah)$ and $T_a^Rf(h)=f(ha)$ are $B$-linear isometries of $C(K,B)$: translations are continuous bijections with continuous inverse, and each supremum is over all of $K$. They preserve $D$, and step 3 shows that the continuous linear maps $I_K\circ T_a^L$ and $I_K\circ T_a^R$ both restrict to $A$ there. The uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-dense-subspace-contractive-extension], applied to the same $D,A,E,F$, identifies both with $I_K$. This proves both translation identities on all continuous functions.

proof.text:
Let $P$ be profinite and $f:P\times K\to B$ continuous. Define $J_P(f)(p)=I_K(f(p,-))$; each section $f(p,-)$ is continuous by restriction of $f$. To prove continuity fix $p_0\in P$ and $\epsilon>0$. The function $d(p,h)=f(p,h)-f(p_0,h)$ is continuous and $d(p_0,h)=0$. For each $h\in K$, continuity gives product neighbourhoods $V_h$ of $p_0$ and $W_h$ of $h$ on which $|d|<\epsilon/2$. Choose finitely many $W_{h_i}$ covering compact $K$, and take $V=\bigcap_iV_{h_i}$. For $p\in V$, every $h$ belongs to one of these $W_{h_i}$, so $\|f(p,-)-f(p_0,-)\|_\infty\leq\epsilon/2$. By linearity and the bound from step 6,
$$|J_P(f)(p)-J_P(f)(p_0)|\leq\|f(p,-)-f(p_0,-)\|_\infty\leq\epsilon/2<\epsilon.$$
This is continuity at $p_0$. For $P=\varnothing$ the assertion is vacuous. This finite-subcover argument checks the parameter topology directly; it assumes neither local compactness of $B$ nor metrizability of $P$ or $K$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image scalar tame-kernel input; agent analytic expansion: continuity in every profinite parameter by an explicit product-neighbourhood argument. The blueprint provides the context, not this argument.

proof.text:
For $c\in C(P,B)$, evaluate at $p$: $J_P(cf)(p)=I_K(c(p)f(p,-))=c(p)I_K(f(p,-))$. Likewise $J_P(f_1+f_2)(p)=J_P(f_1)(p)+J_P(f_2)(p)$ and $J_P(0)=0$, by the established $B$-linearity. The products and sums here are continuous by continuity of the field operations, and step 8 ensures the outputs lie in $C(P,B)$. Thus $J_P$ is $C(P,B)$-linear and commutes with finite sums, including the empty sum. For any continuous $u:P'\to P$ the equality
$$J_{P'}(f\circ(u\times\mathrm{id}_K))(p')=I_K(f(u(p'),-))=(J_P(f)\circ u)(p')$$
holds by the defining evaluation formula. Precomposition preserves continuity because composites of continuous maps are continuous. Equality at every $p'$ proves naturality, also for an empty source. All function sets, finite quotients and their subspaces are taken inside the universes fixed by [def-weil-size-convention].
